intro: The PASS — Pediatric Asthma Severity Score is a respiratory scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Three-item bedside severity score for an asthma exacerbation. It scores 3 criteria and interprets the total across 3 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in respiratory
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 3 criteria: Wheezing; Work of breathing / retractions; Prolonged expiration. Totals are then banded: any score - Mild: pASS 0-1 - mild exacerbation. Short-acting beta-agonist and reassess; 2 points or more - Moderate: pASS 2-3 - moderate exacerbation. Bronchodilators plus systemic corticosteroid; 4 points or more - Severe: pASS 4-6 - severe exacerbation. Intensive bronchodilator therapy, steroids, oxygen, consider magnesium and admission.
guidelineRefs: Source: Gorelick MH et al. Performance of a novel clinical score, the Pediatric Asthma Severity Score (PASS). Acad Emerg Med 2004;11:10-18.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the PASS — Pediatric Asthma Severity Score use?
faqs.a: 3. They are Wheezing; Work of breathing / retractions; Prolonged expiration.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the PASS — Pediatric Asthma Severity Score mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: any score - Mild: pASS 0-1 - mild exacerbation. Short-acting beta-agonist and reassess; 2 points or more - Moderate: pASS 2-3 - moderate exacerbation. Bronchodilators plus systemic corticosteroid; 4 points or more - Severe: pASS 4-6 - severe exacerbation. Intensive bronchodilator therapy, steroids, oxygen, consider magnesium and admission.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?

faqs.a: Yes. Score definitions are bundled with the PediAid app, so the score computes without a connection.
